name: TPU XLA compilation: static shapes, padding, and fusion
arithmetic_intensity: XLA compiles the entire HLO graph to a TPU executable at compile time. All tensor shapes must be known statically — there is no dynamic shape support. The compiler pads tensors to 128x8 chunks (the MXU tile size); padding wastes compute and memory. Batch size must be a multiple of 64 (8 per core) with feature dims multiple of 128, OR batch multiple of 1024 with feature dims multiple of 8. Fusion eliminates intermediate HBM round-trips. Broadcasting can force materialization and prevent fusion.
scales_with: batch_size (must be multiple of 64 or 1024 for efficiency)
tensor_shapes (must be static — no dynamic shapes)
workarounds: Pad tensors to multiples of 128 (feature) and 64/1024 (batch) to avoid XLA padding waste
Use jax.jit with static_argnums to force recompilation per shape rather than dynamic shapes
Structure data to tile into 128x8 chunks natively
Avoid broadcasting patterns that prevent fusion (e.g., argmax of broadcast)
Use XLA flags to control fusion behavior
notes: The TPU performance guide explicitly states: 'To use TPU memory efficiently, structure your data so that it can be tiled into 128 x 8 chunks.' Padding has two drawbacks: (1) under-utilizes the TPU core, (2) increases on-chip memory and can cause OOM. The XLA compiler automatically pads when needed, but well-chosen dimensions avoid it. For v6e+, MXU is 256x256 (up from 128x128), so the minimum efficient GEMM dimension doubled. This is the single most important TPU-specific optimization: shape your model and batch to the hardware tile size.
